name: Woody House
detail: Rooms are clean, hotel is safe and staff kind and attentive.

name: Regal Airport Hotel
detail: I was only there one day but could see that it is a top-class hotel. It has al the mod-cons in the room including a massive LED TV with a welcoming message for you and even speakers in the bathroom. Going to this hotel also really helped as I arrived at about 1am in Hong Kong and so didn't need to look for taxis or late-night transport and then hassle with check-ins in Hong Kong City. Most times you can only check in after 2pm anyway. And the good thing is it is not any more expensive than the normal (and usually much smaller) hotels in Hong Kong City.

name: Ramada Hong Kong Harbour View
detail: I would say it is the Best Price ever if you would like to have a short stay in Hong Kong only for some good sleeping time every night. The location is fantastic. You can walk to Centre. The variety and food around the hotel are good and value for money. Hong Kong is small! You can not expect to have a large room like when you are doing a budget traveling in United States of America. Definitely worth it even though the space is small but, it is the best price ever in Hong Kong in a 4-star hotel. Good customer service! Excellent!

name: Harbour Plaza 8 Degrees
detail: We came through Hong Kong for business. Two families, each with an infant. What we wanted was a hotel in Hong Kong that was decently priced and had a swimming pool for the children. This hotel is well-designed and well-maintained. Front desk staff are very professional. There is an hourly shuttle which takes you to/from Tsim Sha Tsui (Peninsula Hotel). In our opinion, the best part about the hotel was the large and beautiful swimming pool. There is a shallow kid's pool which was excellent for the children to play in.
area: Kowloon City,Hong Kong - View on map

name: Burlington Hotel
detail: The Burlington was a pleasant surprise! Most hotels in Hong Kong are expensive and relatively small, and this was small, but it was great quality at a great price. It was very clean, comfortable, and modern. The staff were friendly, helpful, and very efficient! It’s in a great location on Hong Kong Island, and it was a really easy getting from the airport because the bus (A22) practically drops off right in front of the hotel! And it’s only like a 10-15 minute walk to the Hong Kong Convention Center. There are a ton of nice, cheap places to eat, a very convenient place to stay. I especially appreciated the complimentary Handy phone they include in every room, a cellphone with 4G that was super nice to have for navigation and communication while going around the city...much better than buying a sim and worrying about reception and running out of data. Overall, we were very pleased, and hope to stay at The Burlington again when we go back HK.

name: Harbour Plaza North Point
detail: It was our first time in Hong Kong so we decided to get a 4 Star Hotel. After arriving at Hong Kong airport it took us a few minutes to find the Harbour Center Counter, but after we found it, we felt taken care of already. Cost us HKD$140 each for the airport shuttle to the Hotel, it was a fairly large bus, and it only seated a few of us. This is where we learned that the Airport Shuttle caters to other hotels too. Think of it this way, if you have large bags or luggage, a few bucks is worth it when going to and from the airport because you are going to walk a lot. My bag was a large duffle and it was 24 lbs. and I was so grateful I opted for the shuttle going to and from the Airport. Plus, you get to see Hong Kong more from the bus, unlike when you take the train which goes into the subway after the first 5-6 stations. When we arrived at the hotel, check in was a breeze, they just get the impression of my card and thats it, there was someone who helped us get our things from the bus to the check in counter then from the check-in counter to our room. But be sure to give a separate tip to the one who carries your bag from the bus to the hotel, because it will be a different person who will bring your bags up. The room was quite big/clean compared to other Hotels our friends stayed at. Their's were around 21 sq mts, ours was about 28 sq mts. they were complaining that they had traffic going to and from their bathrooms, while we were comfortable in a King sized bed, we had a stocked mini ref and we had cable. Only problem is internet costed around a HK$100/day. We only stayed at the hotel to sleep and bathe mostly, but we would've loved to use the gym and the pool. Both were clean and complete. Maybe because there are monthly tenants staying at the serviced suites of the hotel. They had a sauna but I didn't get to use it. My girlfriend was able to use the pool, her only complaint was that it wasn't heated. We are coming back, soon.

name: The Kowloon Hotel
detail: i stayed in kowloon on 8 different occasions and all rooms in hong kong/kowloon are small, enough space to move around the bed/s, a small passage to the bathroom and a table/dresser. the kowloon hotel is the same: a small room but very nicely furnished and good equipped. the location of this hotel is of the best, when you walk out on the street the entrance to the train station is a few meters (less than a 100 meters and less than a half minute walk). it is the corner of nathan street and the lobby is breath talking beautiful and stylish, so is the rest of the interior of this hotel. the shower did have hot water every time i want to shower and the linen was crisp, new and clean. when in nathan street and you are looking towards the pier you can see some of the night light displays, but obviously it would be best to see it on the pier or in a bout in the middle between kowloon and hong kong island. when visiting hong kong again i would definitely not stay in any of the two other hotels i stayed previously as this is by far hands down the best and in the same price class as the other i already stayed in.

name: Mini Central
detail: It was quite a walk up the steep slopes and stairs, but hey, it is hong kong after all right? Though the hotel was found sandwiched between two other building, it stood out due to it's small build making it easy to find. Entering the hotel, we were greeted with a very beautifully lobby area which was furnished with modern and contemporary furniture. There were two imacs available for use and even a piano, which i was very much tempted to play but my next to zero instrumental skills prevented me. We were briskly checked in and showed to our room by the efficient, if not so friendly, staffs there. We weren't exactly shocked by the size of the room, having done our research prior to booking the room. In fact, i actually felt that it was better than i'd expected it to be! It would've been very annoying to move around if we had brought big luggages but we were only travelling with backpacks so it wasn't really much of a hassle for us! Besides, when you're in hong kong you wouldn't be staying in that much since there's lots to do. Aside from that, i actually like the fact that the toilet had clear glass walls. It allowed me to watch the telly, not that there was anything to watch actually considering the limited channels they have, and go about my big business all at the same time. Also, toiletries was not provided but can be easily bought from a dispenser at the ground floor, Overall, we're really satisfied with our stay there. It was a really nice hotel with an affordable price. Unless you really don't enjoy small spaces i'm pretty sure you'll like the place! Well, we definitely did and wouldn't mind coming back if i were to visit hong kong again!

name: Ibis Hong Kong North Point
detail: This was the third time that we have stayed at the Ibis North Point and I happily give it five stars – bearing in mind that it is a budget hotel. The room is small but appears to have been designed by someone with experience in designing caravans or river boats. Sufficient storage is tucked away, all with recessed handles so nothing catches as you walk past. There is a safe, tea/coffee making facilities, a hair drier. Fast and free internet is available and there is a flat screen TV, which we never used. The lighting is brilliant. The bed is comfortable, with a double bed rather than twins there is a bit more floor space. The desk is just wide enough for a laptop with two power plugs at desk level and a third below the desk; no grovelling required. Some people may find it difficult to work as the desk is at the window and the window looks out onto Hong Kong harbour! For this view at the Mandarin Oriental you would be paying over $5,000 a night. Unfortunately if you want to enjoy the view you will have to go soon; foundations are going in across the road and my guess would be that a year from now there will be no view. The bathroom is probably a little smaller than the one we had on our last river cruise, but it works really well. My only criticism is that there is no power point, but that may be Hong Kong building regulations rather than the hotel. The towels were big and new. The Staff were great, on the three mornings we went down to breakfast then returned to the room it had been made up whilst we were away. I have eaten much worse breakfast buffets at very expensive hotels. There wasn’t a lot of variety, but there was plenty of food and crucially it was always hot! North Point is perhaps a little away from things, but the entrance to the Mass Transit is less than 50 metres away and once on that you can go anywhere in Hong Kong.
